Masters in Agriculture

A master's degree in agriculture can make you eligible for a wide variety of jobs. From private organizations to government agencies, from being an agronomist to a policy manager - the possibilities are infinite. So what should you do and in which country should you get your master's degree in agriculture from?

Read on to know more about this field that has recently been growing in Popularity. Whether you want to apply for a program or simply want to prepare for the exams for a master's in agriculture in USA and other countries, this page will help.


What information does this page provide me with?

This page provides you with information on pursuing master's programs in agriculture in Australia, Canada, Germany, and the USA. Beyond this, we will also look at some prospective positions and jobs you might be able to secure after graduating with a master's degree in agriculture.

What Countries are Good for Masters in Agriculture?

For Indian students, there are 4 prime options - Australia, Canada, Germany, and the USA. While the countries here are listed alphabetically, each has created its own niche in terms of advanced degrees in education.

Let us look at what each of these countries has to offer, in brief.

Australia

One of the top Argicultural Exporters

Australia is home to some of the best universities for Agriculture in the world. With almost two thirds of the continent covered in desert, agriculture and farming are very important for the nation to maintain self-sufficiency.

Australia is also known for its farming practices, and animal rearing. Australia has taken advantage of its abundant wild-life resources. From rearing Ostriches to Kangaroos, there is little that the country does not take advantage of!


What are some Australian universities?

Of the many good universities, the top three for agriculture would be Universty of Melbourne, University of Sydney, and University of Queensland.

But these are not your only options. There are other lesser known but equally worthy options like the University of Western Australia. If you wish to know more about what university fits your profile the best, Speak to our experts for tailored recommendations!

Canada

8th Largest Argi Exporter in the World

Agriculture is one of the most important industries in Canada. In fact, Canada generates an average of $65bn from argi-exports. Yes, sixty-five billion dollars!

Canada has a respected and recognised animal husbandry industry, which is also good news for those who want to pursue veterinary science. Apart from that, many universities in Canada have good programs and offer abundant research opportunities for those who are interested.


Name some good Canadian universities?

You might not have heard of many of these, but if you wish to pursue a masters program in argicultre, you should not miss looking at University of Guelph, University of McGill and also Ontario Agricultural College.

Beyond this, there are options like the Dalhousie University and University of Lethbridge. If you wish to apply for any masters program in Canada (Agriculture included), our experts will love to help you with recommendations!


👇 Next Country : 🇩🇪 Germany

Germany

For use of technology in Agriculture

Being a country that has always been short on space, Germany has been known to make up for its lack through inventive and ingenious use of technology.

Agriculture courses in Germany are no different. They focus on use of technology. Most universities offer advanced courses in agriculture that look at increasing yield through application of scientific methods.


Which German universities are good for agriculture?

One of the best universities in Germany, TUM (Technical University of Munich / Technische Universität München) offers fantastic master's level programs in agriculture. Also worth considering are the Ludwig Maximilian's University and University of Bonn.

For those that love the countryside and want to bask in the pristine glory of pastoral German towns, look at University of Gottingen. For more programs and universities in Germany, talk to our experts now!


👇 Next Country : 🇺🇸 USA

The USA

Home to the largest number of universities.

If there is one thing the United States of America is famous for, it is super-sizing. The universities and the course choices are no exception. If you are looking for the most number of options, US will probably be your only stop.

It has a wide range of courses, universities that are located in climatic zones that suit your preferences. There is also the aspect of good scholarships and job opportunities.


Can you name some universities?

If you are looking for the best universities for a masters program in agriculture in the USA, among your first options should be the University of Florida, Michigan State University, University of Maryland College Park and Mississippi State University.

But again, remember that there are over 5000 univesities in the US. So your options are wide open. There are several hundred universities that are waiting for your consideration. If you are looking for going to a specific state, program, or a city, Speak to our experts and get a tailor made solution for you!

What kind of Jobs will I get?

Sonme are options that you might not even have imagined existed.

For many from India, agriculture is an area with limited scope. Most do not think beyonf farming, animal husbandry or may be stretch towards veterinary science. In most advanced countries, agriculture is recognised for what it is, and it is treated as any other discipline. There is a lot of research and focus on development.

Here are some of the positions you could be looking at filling once you graduate from your master's program.

  • Biochemist
  • Agricultural Consultant
  • Plant Pathologists
  • Agri-Business
  • Agri-Economists
  • Soil Scientist
  • Rural Practice Surveyor
  • Agronomist
  • Agricultural Engineer
  • Agricultural Manager
  • Livestock Manager
  • Policy Manager
  • Agriculture specialist
  • Global Sustainability specialist
  • Research Scientist
  • Agriculture inspector
  • Agronomist
  • Horticulture Technician
  • Regulatory and quality specialist
  • Hydrogeologist
